A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Concerto research work, with 19 readable pages including Appendices A and B. Text, equations, tables, figures, and rendered pages support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Concerto experiments on semantic and instance segmentation, language probing, and ablations, plus appendix experiments with alternative image encoders and LoRA.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experimental results in the main text and appendices, including Tables 1–6 and 9–11.

M1.justification: The self-distillation and cross-modal prediction procedures, objectives, and components are unchanged. Table 3's revised parameter count does not establish an architectural or algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: Training datasets, segmentation benchmarks, video-lifted scenarios, and language-localization tasks are identical, including the appendix coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the tables, including DINOv2, Sonata, their feature concatenation, and the appendix comparisons involving SigLIP2, RADIO, and adaptation methods.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes the smallest evaluated model's reported size from 16M(T) to 5M(T). This is a limited revision to a stated experimental setting; it does not establish that experiments were rerun. Other settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The ablation questions and outcomes in Table 6, appendix encoder and LoRA analyses, and qualitative case studies are retained. The isolated model-size entry revision provides no additional analytical experiment or outcome.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seed reporting, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises the reported size–performance association by replacing 16M with 5M for model T. Its mIoU values remain 67.7, 24.9, 33.7, and 65.2 across the four benchmarks. All performance scores and qualitative findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical content is identical, including Appendix A.2's projection equation and depth-based visibility condition. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about joint 2D–3D representations, benchmark performance, video perception, and language alignment.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the frozen image encoder, shallow language alignment, and need for broader point-cloud domain coverage. The parameter-count revision receives no explanatory discussion.

D1.justification: Table 3 revises one technical specification: model T's parameter count changes from 16M to 5M. Appendix implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training time, data processing, and access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are identical, including Section 5's relationships to Sonata, DINOv2, and earlier joint 2D–3D approaches.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 27 October 2025 to v2 dated 28 February 2026. Prose, terminology, headings, and document structure are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, table structures, captions, and page layout are unchanged. Table 3's isolated numerical edit does not redesign the display; all embedded figure images match.

improvement.justification: The only scientific edit changes Table 3's T-model size from 16M to 5M while retaining every performance score. This could improve reporting accuracy, but neither PDF explains the revision or provides architectural details that substantiate the new count. With all other content, including appendices, unchanged, the direction of any quality effect cannot be reliably established.
